fields.AN_Notes: Three studies with ChatGPT 3.5 and 4o: cultural value scales (Study 1), 13 one-round decision tasks with country personas and country interactants (Study 2), four prompt strategies as intervention (Study 3). Role_Persona: 'If you are an ordinary individual from [the country]' as instrument; General_Guidance covers the debiasing cues 'From a fairness perspective,', 'As an independent individual, please make a choice according to your own ideas and', 'If you live in a future world.' and 'Imagine you live in a multicultural world,'. Evaluated: the prompt strategies reduced country differences to non-significance in most tested task-model combinations, but the personal-preference prompt failed in the GPT-4o public goods game (own experiment). Axes coded as the work names them, countries/nationality and cultural groups. Direct_Discrimination: allocation decisions (dictator, ultimatum, public goods) toward interactants vary with the nationality stated in the prompt; these are simulated game allocations, not real decisions about persons. Training-data and oversight recommendations in the discussion are outlook and not coded as stages. Theory: Hofstede's cultural dimensions and GLOBE dimensions frame the explanation of the bias sources. Gender appears only as the GLOBE dimension gender egalitarianism, not as an object.

fields.AN_Notes: Multilingual and multicultural prompting: several prompt variants with language and cultural cues (e.g. 'You are a Chinese-speaking assistant', persona with name, birthplace, favourite food), responses combined by concatenation (Ensembling) and compared against high temperature, requesting diversity, random personas and step-by-step recall on GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, LLaMA 70B and 8B. Evaluated: multilingual prompting yields the highest normalized entropy in most comparisons and lowers hallucination of culture-specific names in a human annotation study (own experiment). The work frames the problem as lack of diversity and unequal exposure rather than as bias; its understanding of bias is recognisable only from the entropy measures. Axes: nationality, ethnicity and region of generated names, cultural and language perspectives on social norms. Harm types from the own experiment: American default in named artists (Exclusionary_Norms) and overlooking underrepresented cultural backgrounds (Erasure). Gender appears only in a persona cue and a social-norm example.

fields.AN_Notes: Inclusive prompt engineering for DALL-E portraits as a three-step method: define focal point with demographic descriptors, view the descriptors DALL-E adds to the prompt, alter the text using the AI-provided structure. General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'reinforcing particularly important traits several times with various synonyms' and 'Using the AIprovided prompt as a general template for future prompts'. Zero-shot prompting serves as research instrument to expose the model's defaults. Demonstrated: the method is applied and shown on example images without a systematic evaluation. Other_Task: visual content design for social media, interfaces and personas by content designers and technical communicators; the teaching implication is coded as Learning_Content. Axes from own case studies: low-income couple turned white (Race_Ethnicity, Socioeconomic), 65-year-old woman (Age), body size and baldness (Physical_Appearance), disability as appearance treated as negative (Disability), default young thin white man (Gender). No passage makes an outcome depend on a combination of axes. Gender appears as binary descriptor (woman, man) without determination. Bias definition: the work determines its own bias mechanism 'toxic positivity'. Theories: social justice approach in technical communication (Walton, Moore, Jones) and tactical technical communication.

fields.AN_Notes: Feminist legal reading of the EU AI Act along pre-market regulation, provider responsibilities and deployer obligations. Proposed measures: intersectional bias audits, gender impact assessment within the fundamental rights impact assessment, diverse auditing and development teams, participation of affected communities, independent oversight bodies (Organisational_Process), diverse and representative datasets in standardisation (Pre_Processing); all remain proposals. Axes from the own argument: gender including trans, non-binary and intersex identities, race, sexual orientation and gender identity, socioeconomic status in the SyRI analysis; Intersectional through the SyRI case and the woman-of-colour argument. Harm types: binary and male-default norms in the AI Act and in algorithmic decision-making (Exclusionary_Norms), the author's Google Translate example (Stereotyping), SyRI welfare-fraud flagging via historical data and income (Indirect_Discrimination); the hiring and healthcare cases are cited from other work and not coded separately. Population and task: the object is EU AI law in general; SyRI (social welfare fraud detection) is one worked case, so Social_Assistance_Admin and a welfare decision task are not coded as the addressed setting. Bias is framed structurally through the theories but not determined in a sentence of its own. Theories frame gender and bias explicitly: Fricker's hermeneutical injustice, MacKinnon's dominance theory, intersectionality (Cooper, Crenshaw), Quijano's coloniality of power, Mignolo's decoloniality, queer theory.

fields.AN_Notes: AI literacy framework for K-12 education with three modes of engagement (Understand, Evaluate, Use), six AI literacy practices, core values Centering Human Judgment and Centering Justice, three types of use, and five strategies for school systems. Prompting is a learning practice ('Distinguish between essential and nonessential components of a prompt to produce an appropriate output') and a classroom practice (AI prompt organizer in a special education class). General_Guidance strategy verbatim: 'Effectively prompting a GenAI system or tool takes time and often requires clear communication, specificity, experimentation, and patience'. Axes from the own worked example of a GenAI image of a doctor as a white male; the race, age and gender examples of children's findings and the proxy-variable example (zip code) are cited from other work and not coded. Harm: Stereotyping from the doctor example; Indirect_Discrimination via proxies is attributed to cited work and left uncoded. Mitigation: AI literacy, professional learning, adoption guidance, inclusive policy and human oversight (Organisational_Process), proposed; district case examples illustrate AI literacy programmes, not a bias-mitigation evaluation. Population: K-12 students, teachers and families, outside social work. Task: AI use for lesson planning, content creation, grading and scaffolded writing. Gender appears as binary categories (females, white male) without determination. The justice perspective cites literature on algorithmic bias and 'tech justice' but names no theory that frames bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Hand-built QA bias benchmark with ambiguous and disambiguated contexts for nine social dimensions and two intersectional categories (race by gender, race by SES), tested zero-shot on UnifiedQA, RoBERTa and DeBERTaV3. The templated contexts and questions serve as input instruments to elicit bias; no prompting technique is named. Generative_KI coded ja because the work frames its object as large language models; RoBERTa and DeBERTaV3 are encoder models fine-tuned for multiple choice, UnifiedQA generates strings. All nine axes are measured; Intersectional rests on the race-by-SES and race-by-gender breakdowns, which the authors describe as mixed and suggestive. Harm: Stereotyping (stereotype reinforcement and attribution); the accuracy gap between bias-aligned and non-aligned answers is a stereotype effect, not a quality difference between groups, so Disparate_Performance is not coded. No mitigation: 'This work does not directly contribute to debiasing or other harm reduction measures'. Gender categories man/woman, girl/boy and census male/female names. Bias definition adopted explicitly from Crawford's representational harms; this definition is not counted again as a theory reference.
